prompt_en: A photograph of a mecha subject: a mechanical structure with an open-front cockpit above two compact articulated walking legs, parked in a quiet outdoor proving yard. In the frame, the mechanical subject is visibly present as a substantial working machine with joints, overlapping plates and worn load-bearing feet. A pilot sits in the cockpit, pausing over a folded route map before setting off. Use the supplied portrait as the pilot's facial and hair appearance reference. Preserve brown eyes and softly rounded facial contours, with a short dark brown bob, wispy separated bangs. Her face has a calm, concentrated presence in the soft daylight. The pilot rests her anatomical LEFT forearm along the left cockpit sill; her anatomical RIGHT hand lies flat on the paper route map. The map rests on her right thigh. The left cockpit sill is a broad horizontal support under the full left forearm. The paper route map shows a route line across its paper surface. The folded sheet has visible paper edges beneath her palm. Seen from the front, her left forearm and sill are on image right, while her right hand, map and right thigh are on image left. Her shoulders, elbows, wrists and fingers form relaxed, traceable chains. The seat supports her pelvis and back, and both boot soles are planted on the shallow open-front cockpit floor, with their sole-to-floor contacts exposed below her knees. The machine's two walking legs are separated in projection from hip joints through knees and ankles to two broad feet resting flat on the yard surface. A low front rim keeps the pilot's boot contacts in view. Frame the complete compact machine from a mildly elevated, almost frontal viewpoint, including the pilot's face, both arm contacts, the cockpit floor, both complete machine legs and both ground contacts together, with a small margin of ground below the feet. Let a 50mm-equivalent photographic view, clear midtone daylight and deep usable focus make the human pause and the machine's weight equally tangible. Her practical sand-colored work suit and the machine's pale worn metal belong to the same restrained, credible field scene.

h_f2_material_decisions.rationale: Review 1: Giant piloted mecha, cockpit canopy, limbs and armor with operator relationship. The baseline already realizes cockpit/limbs/operator but deliberately uses compact proportions. A giant-scale variant would reduce pilot contact size in full-support framing. The engineering-office alternative explores scale contrast; compact final is preferred for repair readability, not because size is user-locked. See composition-comparison.md.

Review 2: Selected human elbows contact assigned knees/thighs with a readable load path and seated support. The pilot left forearm must remain along the sill, so both elbows-on-knees would alter that same actor contact. A machine elbow does not inherit this human source. No partial load-path-only adoption. See composition-comparison.md.

Review 3: Human forward lunge with rear leg extended and rear knee off floor. A standing or deeply split human stance changes the repaired seated two-boot support. Rebuilding a long cockpit to combine a lunge with sill/map contacts offers no restrained improvement over the quiet seated state; mechanical legs are different owners and are not this human cue. See composition-comparison.md.

Review 4: Human palm braces on sitting surface beside/behind pelvis, with connected arm and seated support. A pilot palm cannot move from the map/sill interaction to a seat brace as a repair. Each component remains optional but generic coherent arms already predate this source; none is selected. See composition-comparison.md.

Review 5: Retire bundle: one leg supports, other knee folds open, working foot near support knee, support foot visible. The lifted foot leaves the repaired pair of cockpit-floor contacts. The source is not recast as a machine leg pose; no selected child or profile activation. See composition-comparison.md.

Review 5: Retire bundle: one leg supports, other knee folds open, working foot near support knee, support foot visible. The lifted foot leaves the repaired pair of cockpit-floor contacts. The source is not recast as a machine leg pose; no selected child or profile activation. See composition-comparison.md.

Review 6: Chair straddle keeps pelvis on seat, one leg on each side and visible supports. REST realizes a narrow saddle and two boot-floor supports. This is compatible, but human leg separation, torso wrap and harness increase contour density around the map. The final simpler seat configuration makes ownership easier to trace. See composition-comparison.md.

Review 7: Complete adult M-leg profile: low pelvis, raised bent knees, connected legs, supported feet and already frontal M silhouette. The explicit adult prerequisite is absent from the frozen requester facts. Generic support is only partial; the camera is not changed to force an unrequested M silhouette. The separate same-geometry slot source 25 is reviewed on its own conditions. See composition-comparison.md.

Review 8: One human leg is principal support; free leg has relaxed/light contact and pelvis/torso sit over that base. The pilot is carried by seat/back and two floor contacts, not a standing single-leg body support. A visual weight shift would not prove its load relation. No transfer of human morphology to machine legs. See composition-comparison.md.

Review 9: Human mecha pilot cosplay performer. Performer identity would change the photograph into a costume presentation unless the mechanical subject still remains explicit. No reference identity or occupation is inferred; existing pilot presence already supplies the visible human relation without a cosplay claim. See composition-comparison.md.

Review 9: Human mecha pilot cosplay performer. Performer identity would change the photograph into a costume presentation unless the mechanical subject still remains explicit. No reference identity or occupation is inferred; existing pilot presence already supplies the visible human relation without a cosplay claim. See composition-comparison.md.

Review 10: Floor-supported pelvis with both folded legs to one side and traceable knees/ankles. This human floor configuration substitutes folded leg support for the repaired seat and two exposed boot soles. It is not a machine kneeling instruction; no adoption. See composition-comparison.md.

Review 11: Fixed supported camera self portrait with timer/remote while actor hands retain their own roles. A timer could coexist with both pilot hand contacts, but it supplies no distinct visible change when the capture device is outside the frame. Operator/timer history is not pixel evidence. The final camera remains an authorial capture choice without a self-portrait claim. See composition-comparison.md.

Review 12: Human palm/forearm against wall, with own elbow-wrist direction and separate wall endpoint. The protected left forearm target is the horizontal cockpit sill, not a wall. A wall substitute would transfer that meaningful contact. Generic support geometry already exists independently. See composition-comparison.md.

Review 13: Full head-to-feet frame plus support-leg stance, relaxed other leg and connected shoulder/pelvis weight shift. Full pilot and machine support inclusion is already in the baseline. The additional single-leg stance is not the seated support state. Selecting only the generic framing part would not adopt this complete stance bundle; no distinct improvement is retained. See composition-comparison.md.

Review 14: Hand directed toward another existing actor face across a visible gap with both boundaries. A second human face is not frozen, and the pilot hands already contact sill and map. No new face or hand transfer is introduced; an asserted gap is not visible proof. See composition-comparison.md.

Review 15: Sheet wraps selected torso, held by hands or declared mechanism; clear coverage with independent clothing state. REST uses a shoulder clasp to hold the torso sheet while preserving both pilot arm contacts and work clothing. It can add intimacy and a reason for the pause, but wrap/harness boundaries compete with the map and silhouette. Final clear work suit is preferred after that complete alternative. See composition-comparison.md.

Review 16: Stable floor-level capture device below actor, with continuous floor beneath camera and actor. At yard-floor height the lens lies below the raised cockpit floor and loses its top plane and boot support boundaries. The final independent mildly elevated view exposes those consequential endpoints. The low camera source is skipped, not partially adopted as generic stability. See composition-comparison.md.

Review 17: Same-jacket panel has opposed diagonals, offset contact points and continuous structure inside seam; optional members cumulative only if chosen. REST realizes the jacket panel and seam. It adds tactile specificity, but its directional pattern competes with route-map graphics in the same central area. The selected plain suit preserves hierarchy. See composition-comparison.md.

Review 18: Facing is a partial inner lining folded inward and attached to a neckline/armhole edge, not another garment. REST shows a joined inward neckline facing on the open jacket. This could be coherent, but its small inside seam is peripheral at full-machine scale and adds little to the repaired interaction; omitted from final. See composition-comparison.md.

Review 19: Insurance claims investigation office. ENGINEERING-OFFICE places the compact machine within a high-ceilinged claims office with files and desk. It creates an interesting machine/bureaucracy scale contrast, but background objects and indoor depth compete with support boundaries. The quiet yard better isolates the same human-machine pause. See composition-comparison.md.

Review 20: Same bodysuit mesh, satin straps and buckle with explicit layer order, continuity and incoming strap endpoints. This compound lingerie material treatment would add a separate erotic wardrobe focus against fetish 0 and the restrained field direction. Generic harness detail is not borrowed from its fishnet/satin/buckle relation. No selected members. See composition-comparison.md.

Review 21: Wreck survey joins anomaly reading, observed site and operator; primary treasure/search context required. No primary search/treasure or wreck/anomaly evidence is frozen. The paper route map is not a sonar or magnetometer reading; no capture or measurement success is inferred. See composition-comparison.md.

Review 22: Two separate load branches share the same two nodes; complete paths and division junction visible. ENGINEERING-OFFICE makes both branch routes and both nodes visible on an open chassis inspection board. This is a compatible local apparatus alternative, but it creates an additional fine endpoint task beside the already consequential pilot contacts. The final uncluttered chassis gives map and support more visual weight; source unselected. See composition-comparison.md.

Review 23: Continuous flat cloth motif/ground differ by reflection, crossed by the same fold; entire EN/KO relation required. REST realizes it on the torso wrap without claiming fiber, actual weave or history. The fold and reflective motif add soft material contrast, but compete with harness and map. Plain cloth in the final is independently preexisting, not source-derived partial adoption. See composition-comparison.md.

Review 24: Public-use consent, separate histories, measured access gaps and later service incorporation as a procedure. A single still of this pilot/mecha cannot establish that institutional sequence, consent or measured results. No procedure is inferred from papers or used as visual decoration. See composition-comparison.md.

Review 25: Human low seated pelvis between raised bent knees, traceable legs, support and already frontal M outline. This slot source has no adult prerequisite beyond age-context tags, so no adulthood claim is inferred. It still requires the already selected frontal M view and all low-pelvis geometry. Baseline mild three-quarter view and seat height do not establish it; changing the camera solely to force that silhouette is not a repair benefit. See composition-comparison.md.

Review 26: Crossed-shins sitting surface: knees outward, feet beside opposite legs and folded lower legs carried by the seat. The whole configuration relocates boots from cockpit floor to seat. It cannot preserve the two repaired sole-to-floor contacts; generic seat pelvis support is not enough for adoption. See composition-comparison.md.

Review 27: V61 pelvis in seat, straps across chest and independent panel before knees, all EN/KO positives cumulative. REST realizes the harness and separated narrow panel around the same seated pilot. Its extra cockpit detail can clarify a pilot role, but panel and straps crowd the essential boots/map. Final lighter cockpit is preferred, without inferring aircraft, qualification or native approval. See composition-comparison.md.

Review 28: A pilot helmet held under one arm. An under-arm helmet can coexist with the left forearm resting on the sill if tucked above it, but it occupies the exact sill/forearm contour needed for side inspection. It adds no repair benefit and risks obscuring contact; it is not moved to background and claimed as retained. See composition-comparison.md.

Review 29: Used mug within reach beside folded cloth, with stable working surface and clear passage. REST places the mug and separate folded cloth on a cockpit shelf and keeps the floor route clear. This gives a visible break context, but adds a second small prop beside the route map. Final retains the map as the one focal hand-related object; no chronology or invisible recent use is claimed from pixels. See composition-comparison.md.

Review 30: Both hands cup/open beneath chin with separately connected wrists/arms. Both pilot hands would leave their protected map and sill duties. This source is ineligible for that same actor relation; no affect or age is inferred from the hand-pose label. See composition-comparison.md.
